### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only what the customer asked" (hand over the income-loss acceptance now): excluded by the two state-form sentences + records (two approved claims of the same stay unreimbursed -> "not fixed"); and the standard's deductible-borne rule makes the figure depend on that state (250.00 vs 83.333…).
- Lost-income valuation alternative: category_sublimits "How lost income is valued (every level): the nightly subtotal of each confirmed stay the host had to cancel" — gives 1890.00 here, equal to the verified loss, so it does not compete with the standard's "starts from the loss the claims team verified"; reimbursement_conditions marks "its verified loss is the nightly subtotal of the stays the host had to cancel for at most the level's maximum nights" **no longer in force**. The 7-night cap is applied by the lost-nights method; a nightly-rate × 7 reading (210.00 × 7 = 1470.00) coincides here.
- Blocked nights 9 vs 10: protect wording "from the first blocked night to the day after the last blocked night" with record fields `block_start_date`/`block_end_date`; that `block_end_date` is the day after the last night is supported by the record itself (equals the cancelled stay's `check_out_date`, `nights: 9`), by the customer ("nine-night booking") and by the listing product's doc. A 10-night reading would give 1323.00 and 573.87; recorded as a visibility observation, not a defect, since the record and the stay row close it.
- Most recent quality review: 2026-10-01 warning (2026-07-01 also warning) — no alternative changes the tier.
- Property deductible: Professional Host + Entire Home row has "Further condition: none" -> 1.5×, no ledger condition, so P1/P2 order is free.
- Host cancellation band: read as recorded ("30_days_to_48_hours", host) -> 80; recomputing the band from dates is not what the doc asks.
- Level tenure: start `tier_changed_date` 2026-02-16 (not enrollment 2021-03-15); end = host service fee date 2026-08-14 -> 179.
- Composition: all percentages apply "to the lost income being settled, before any guest payment or deductible"; the lost-nights method sets that value first ("The value so set is the lost income being settled"); multiplication commutes; one rounding at the end.
